title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for management of type 2 diabetes and renal function.

HPI
The patient is a 64-year-old male presenting for a routine follow-up of his chronic kidney disease stage 4 and type 2 diabetes mellitus. He reports adherence to his current regimen but notes occasional fatigue. He has been on his current medications for several years. He denies any acute changes in renal function or significant fluctuations in blood glucose levels during home monitoring.

Medication List
- Insulin and an oral hypoglycemic (metformin)
- Vitamin D supplement

Exam
The patient appears well-nourished and in no acute distress. Vital signs are stable. Physical examination reveals no new skin lesions or edema. Renal function is monitored via laboratory results.

Assessment
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus
2. Chronic kidney disease stage 4

Plan
Continue the current regimen of insulin and metformin. Laboratory work will be ordered to monitor renal markers and HbA1c levels. The patient will return to the clinic in three months for a repeat evaluation of his chronic kidney disease stage 4 and diabetes management.
explanations: CKD is listed under 'with' for diabetes in the Index, so the link is presumed: use the combination code E11.22.
Code also the CKD stage (N18.4) as instructed at the diabetes CKD code or separately when unrelated.
When both insulin and oral hypoglycemics are used, assign both Z79.4 and Z79.84.

distractors.why: The provider does not have to write 'due to'; 'with' presumes the link.
E11.2 is a subcategory; a 5th character is required.
The stage of CKD must be reported with N18.-.
Both Z codes are assigned when both drug types are used.
